title: Semantic search
like: "search by meaning" on a help center
brief: A help center lets people type a question in plain words and finds the right articles even when the words differ. Each question is turned into a list of numbers (a vector) and matched to similar articles. Many people ask the same few questions.

clarify.q: How fast must an answer come back?
clarify.a: Under about a second. A person is waiting at the search box.

clarify.q: Do many people ask the same thing?
clarify.a: Yes. About half of all questions repeat within a day.
A few times a day. New articles are searchable within minutes.

notes: About 50,000 articles, each stored as one vector (approx.).
Making a vector takes about 30 ms on a small model server (approx.).

numbers.label: Searches that need a new vector with half repeating

hints: Half of the questions repeat. Do you need to turn each into a vector again?
A cache keyed on the question saves the vector work. Put article vectors in a vector database for the matching.
Load balancer, servers, cache for repeated questions, embedding service, vector database.

editorial.summary: The costly step is turning a question into a vector. Remember answers to repeated questions and that step disappears for half the traffic. The matching itself is one lookup in a vector database that fits in memory.

designs.name: Remember repeated questions
designs.why: A cache returns the saved results for a question that has been seen. Only new questions reach the embedding service, and the vector database finds the nearest articles.

tradeoffs: A longer cache time saves model work, but a changed article may not show for an hour.
A bigger model finds better matches and costs more per question. A small one is usually enough for a help center.
Match by meaning and by words together for the best results. Either alone misses some cases.
New articles need a vector made once, in the background.
editorial.realWorld: Making a vector with a small model takes tens of milliseconds, and a vector database finds nearest matches in a few milliseconds over a hundred thousand items (approx.). Repeated questions make caching worthwhile.
